claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch based on aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and a monitored reversible 6% rollout, provided the exposed aviation maintenance triage limitation and rollout context are explicitly disclosed in the model card.
decision_criteria: Aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents support general launch readiness but do not alone satisfy model-card disclosure policy.
If the affected use case remains exposed, rollout controls help only if there is completed disclosure or reviewed risk acceptance.
An approved risk acceptance or finalized model-card disclosure would materially strengthen the certification case.
Without evidence that one of those policy paths is actually satisfied, certification remains under-supported.
evidence_requests: Provide the actual pre-launch model card or release artifact showing explicit disclosure of the aviation maintenance triage limitation and rollout monitoring context.
Provide any approved risk acceptance covering the exposed aviation maintenance triage segment, including approver and rationale.
Provide the final launch checklist or certification record showing the disclosure requirement was satisfied before launch.
specific_concerns: The affected aviation maintenance triage segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The risk acceptance draft is not approved and does not address the aviation maintenance triage exposure.
The policy text says rollout controls do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
The admissible record supports a need for disclosure, but does not show that the required model-card disclosure has actually been completed before launch.
The actor's recommended action is certification, but the required policy predicate for that posture is only described as necessary, not evidenced as satisfied.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant rather than only potentially compliant if disclosure is actually completed before launch.
That rollout controls materially mitigate the disclosure weakness for policy purposes despite the exposed segment remaining in cohort.
That the strongest supportable posture is certification, absent admissible evidence of completed disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
